title: Catalog-aware profile synthesis and stable pinning for benchmark artifacts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Extend the benchmark harness so that model onboarding produces reproducible, catalog-indexed performance profiles and a minimal set of pinned artifacts that can be consumed by runtime rollouts and the Console.

Scope:
- Add a catalog-aware profile synthesizer that groups dataset+prompt+runner variants into canonical profile entries with deterministic IDs.
- Implement a stable pinning scheme (artifact manifest) that captures: model version, tokenizer fingerprint, dataset snapshot id, canonical prompt set, eval-runner shim version, and quantization/compile profile.
- Augment eval runners with a lightweight shim interface so runners can advertise deterministic sampling policies and seed handling.
- Surface publishing metadata to the profile registry (for Console and runtime) including perf percentiles, tail latency, mem/VRAM footprints, and experiment annotations.

Non-goals:
- Full UI work in Console (we will emit registry records; Console work is a follow-up).
- Rewriting existing eval runners; we add a compatible shim adapter.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Running onboarding/harness with --emit-manifest produces a JSON manifest with stable IDs and fingerprints that can be used to re-run the same profile deterministically.
2) Registry record created and can be queried by model_id:model_version to return the published profile and artifact URIs.
3) CI tests verify that seeded runs reproduce median and 95th-percentile latency within configured tolerance for a controlled toy model.

Success metrics:
- Reduce manual interventions for onboarding by 60% (measured by onboarding support tickets).
- Increase repeatable profile re-runs in CI from 40% -> 90% across sampled models.
- Registry query latency < 200ms p95 for published profiles.

Implementation notes / design decisions:
- Prompt fingerprinting: use normalized token-level hash (BLAKE2b-64) after whitespace/quote normalization to avoid transients from formatting.
- Dataset snapshotting: reference dataset ids from the harness catalog (not raw paths) and include an optional git-LFS manifest for non-catalog datasets.
- Stable IDs: compute deterministic canonical key as blake2b( model_id || version || tokenizer-fp || dataset-id || prompt-set-fp || runner-shim-version ). Store base58-encoded id in manifest.
- Sampling policy: runners must expose 'sampling_mode' and 'seed' semantics; for legacy runners we provide a shim adapter that seeds RNGs and logs seed values to the manifest.
- Backwards compatibility: existing consumers expecting older profile formats should continue to work; we emit both legacy profile and new registry_record v2 in manifest for a transition window.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: aligned with Product (R. Patel) on desired console UX. Decided to emit registry v2 records and not block Console rollout.
2026-02-18 - Design review: PO and Runtime lead requested deterministic canonical ID approach instead of UUIDs. Action: use BLAKE2b canonical hashing (Sam to prototype).

2026-02-25 - Prototype: Sam integrated prompt fingerprinting and produced stable IDs for toy-model runs. Observed ~3% variance in 95th percentile across runs caused by sampling mismatch; identified need for runner shim seeding.

2026-03-02 - PR submitted: github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/1842 adds manifest emission and prompt hashing. Needs: unit tests for normalization and spec for manifest schema. @Design requested example manifest for review.

2026-03-05 - Review notes from Design (Maya Lee): Ensure canonical prompt ordering in sets (alphabetical by prompt fingerprint) for deterministic keying; also add human-readable prompt labels for debugability.

2026-03-08 - Engineering follow-up: implemented runner shim interface and adapter for the legacy beam/eval runners. Added seed logging and deterministic sampling_mode enforcement. Integration tests green locally.

2026-03-12 - QA: CI flaky on macos-runner job; flake traced to GOPATH env causing LFS manifest path mismatch. Temporary workaround added; investigating stable fix. QA requests a rollout checklist before publishing profiles to prod registry.
Open TODO: add schema validator and publish contract doc in Confluence; coordinate with Console team to add registry v2 consumption.
notes: Rollout plan: stage in staging registry for two weeks, run golden-model verification, then publish to prod with a feature flag. Post-publish monitoring dashboard to track variance and query errors.
